source.layout: Call of Duty Wiki map pages (all 14 checked), plus callofdutymaps.com for named structures.
source.tactics: Where a map has a ZigZack IGN map-recon walkthrough, the callouts and positions come from that. Otherwise from BO1-era community guides where they exist, and reasoned from the layout where they don't. Each map's 'Checked against the wiki' list says which.
source.confidence: Each map lists what was verified against the wiki under 'Checked against the wiki'. Anything not listed there is inference.
source.images: Map loading art and in-game minimaps from callofdutymaps.com. Game assets are property of Activision/Treyarch and are used here in a non-commercial fan project.

maps.name: Nuketown
maps.identity: Two suburban houses facing each other across a road, with a bus and a truck in between. Nearly symmetrical, one of the smallest maps in the series, and the centre is a warzone you should mostly stay out of.

sides.name: House A
sides.spawn: The back garden behind your house. Don't linger — the gardens turn into killing fields the moment the match starts.
sides.opening: Three ways out: the road down either side of the house, straight through the ground floor, or upstairs. Either rush the opening by the truck in the middle, or take the upper floor. Both are real plans; crossing the open centre is not.
sides.flank: Down the side path past the garage, using the truck for cover.
sides.pinch: The side path by the flowers. It's one of the map's four chokepoints and it's watched from their front garden.

sides.name: House B
sides.spawn: The back garden behind the opposite house. Same warning — move out of it.
sides.opening: Either guard the front garage area to break their rush before it starts, or get to the second floor and hold the window over the centre.
sides.flank: The opposite side path, into their blind side.
sides.pinch: The front door approach. Covered from the upper floor opposite.

powerPositions.name: The upper floor of your own house
powerPositions.why: Elevation over the centre and the other house. Claymore both doorways behind you and you can watch the middle without being in it.

powerPositions.name: The opening by the truck in the centre
powerPositions.why: From here you cover three of the map's four chokepoints at once — the garage, the side path by the garage, and the front door. It's the strongest single spot on the map and most players never take it.

enemySpots.name: Both upper floors
enemySpots.note: Assume one is occupied at all times. The window over the centre is too good to leave empty.

enemySpots.name: Lying in the front-garden grass
enemySpots.note: A known ambush: prone in the grass by the garage, waiting for anyone taking the side path.

enemySpots.name: The garages
enemySpots.note: Each house has one and it covers the side approach — one of the four chokepoints.

maps.trap: Pushing past the bus and the truck. The moment your team is through the middle, the game has nowhere safe left on their end and starts spawning them behind your lines — so the kills you just got become shots in your back. On Nuketown the discipline is to hold your side of the vehicles, not to win the centre.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 19.5m covers the whole map, and a 0.2s aim-in wins the corner fights.
loadout.perkWhy: The map is small enough that explosives are used liberally by everyone, and the two spawns are close enough for an opening grenade to reach.

deeper: Do not use the cars as cover — they explode when damaged, and the person shooting them knows that.
At the start of the match, a short pause and then a grenade lobbed over the house can catch the enemy still leaving their garden. Expect one coming the other way.

The spawn tell: if you're upstairs and see a teammate running from the opposite house, or an enemy appears from beneath you, the spawns have already flipped — turn round and cover the balcony behind you.
Attack helicopters are strong here because there's very little cover from above.
Concussion grenades decide more fights here than guns do. Tactical Mask Pro is a genuine counter.
verified: Two houses, two floors each, with a garage — map is nearly symmetrical (wiki)
Both teams spawn in a back garden area; three routes out: side road, ground floor, or upper floor (wiki)
The centre holds a bus and a truck; sightlines there favour SMGs and ARs (wiki)
The centre is a high-risk warzone best avoided; the two houses are the contested strongholds (community guide)
The opening by the truck controls three of the four chokepoints: garage, side path by the garage, and front door (2011 map guide)
Pushing past the bus causes enemies to respawn behind your lines (2011 map guide)
Cars explode when damaged and should not be used as cover (community guide)
Backyard spawn zones become killing fields immediately after the match starts (community guide)

maps.name: Firing Range
maps.identity: A compact training facility with three routes through it — left flank, middle road, right flank. Two elevated holds, the garage and top wooden, decide most games between them.

sides.name: OP 40 (south)
sides.spawn: The southern end of the map. The garage is directly in front of you.
sides.opening: Take the garage. It's elevated, it watches enemies crossing below, and it's one of the most popular spots on the map — so it's a race. From there you have access to the nook, below the sniper perch.
sides.flank: Garage into the sandbags, then transition into double barrels to watch the left flank with cover. An assault rifle covers that crossing well.
sides.pinch: The shipping container on the way out of the shooting range. Throw a flash or stun over it before you commit.

sides.name: Tropas (north)
sides.spawn: The northern end, by the second shooting range.
sides.opening: Contest top wooden. Controlling it gives your team eyes on most of the map, including top garage — and it has an escape into back alley if it turns.
sides.flank: Out through back alley, or down the side into the sandbags to peek top garage and lower mid.
sides.pinch: Moving through the shooting range itself. It's full of campers and spawn points — be thorough, don't sprint it.

powerPositions.name: Top wooden (the wooden bunker)
powerPositions.why: Eyes on most of the map, including top garage, and a clean escape into back alley. The single most valuable hold here.

powerPositions.name: The garage
powerPositions.why: Elevated over the crossings and one of the most popular spots on the map. Watches enemies moving below and connects to the nook.

enemySpots.name: Top garage
enemySpots.note: Named as a popular spot. Check it from wooden before you cross.

enemySpots.name: The sniper perch and the elevated middle structures
enemySpots.note: The map's sniping positions. Vulnerable to a lobbed grenade and to a knife in the back — which is also how you deal with them.

enemySpots.name: The second shooting range, down back alley
enemySpots.note: Home to many campers and to spawn points.

maps.trap: Moving without checking around you. The map is small and laid out so that the middle road and the crossings are covered from the garage, top wooden and the perch at once — run it blind and you're caught in a crossfire within seconds of spawning. Lower mid in particular is ground that gets peeked from above.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 39.4m covers every sightline here, and an assault rifle is what you want for watching the left flank from the sandbags.
loadout.perkWhy: Spy Planes go up constantly on a map this small, and the flanks only work if they can't see you take them.

deeper: If someone is in the tower, don't duel them — lob a grenade or two up. It's small and enclosed, and that's the intended answer.
If you take an elevated spot, claymore the way up behind you, and don't stay scoped — the standard punishment here is a knife in the back.
Attack helicopters do well because the map offers very little aerial protection.
Snipers struggle: the map is too small for the ranges they need.
Gas into a contested area creates enough confusion to take it.
If you're running a suppressor, the FAMAS drops to a 3-shot kill inside 14m — across the middle that's a 4-shot kill.
verified: Tropas spawn is the northern end of the map; OP 40 spawn is the south (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Three major routes: right flank, middle road, left flank (ZigZack)
The garage sits in front of the OP 40 spawn, is elevated, watches enemies crossing below, and is one of the most popular spots (ZigZack)
The nook sits below the sniper perch and is accessed from the garage (ZigZack)
Sandbags give cover and peek both sides; you can watch the left flank from them and transition into double barrels (ZigZack)
Controlling top wooden gives eyes on most of the map including top garage; sandbags peek top garage or lower mid; wooden escapes to back alley (ZigZack)
Back alley leads to a second shooting range, home to many campers and spawn points (ZigZack)
A choke point sits at the shipping container when exiting the shooting range — flash or stun the spawns beyond it (ZigZack)
Two elevated middle structures are the sniping spots; vulnerable to lobbed grenades and knifing, so claymore your back (Dominate Black Ops)
A bathroom hut in the north-west has two exits with sightlines to critical points (Dominate Black Ops)
Grenades lob into the high central tower reliably (Dominate Black Ops)
Little aerial protection, so helicopter streaks are strong (Dominate Black Ops)
Favours SMGs, ARs and LMGs; shotguns for defending; snipers difficult (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Summit
maps.identity: A small mountain facility built around a central control room. Four major choke points, and every one of them involves that room — so the game is really about who owns the middle and whether you keep the enemy pushed back.

sides.name: Spetsnaz spawn
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side. Check every corner for campers before you move — it's a known problem here.
sides.opening: Push into the control room. On a map this small you have to keep pushing the enemy back, because that's what gives you favourable spawns.
sides.flank: Around or through the electrical room is a quick route to the porch, and a good peek onto people pushing.
sides.pinch: The electrical room route into the porch. It works, but it is a magnet for grenades.

sides.name: Black Ops spawn
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side.
sides.opening: Use the balcony first — it gives a clear view of some major spawn points, which tells you where they are before you commit to anything.
sides.flank: The rock area gives a long-range view down the west side; the skinny bridge from there leads to the back of the Spetsnaz spawn.
sides.pinch: The skinny bridge. Narrow, and good snipers pick players off through the trees around it.

powerPositions.name: Top control room
powerPositions.why: A hot spot and one of the bigger rooms on the map once all the glass is broken. Multiple levels, multiple windows, and about half a dozen entrances to watch.

powerPositions.name: The back area and the back stairs
powerPositions.why: Both named as underused. The back area gives great vision of nearby spawn points; the back stairs punish people who sprint up rather than holding.

enemySpots.name: Bottom control room
enemySpots.note: Where SMG players cruise — a variety of peeks and a lot of traffic.

enemySpots.name: The rock area
enemySpots.note: The sniper route. Any good sniper plays it for the long view down the west side.

enemySpots.name: Corners of the Spetsnaz spawn, and the porch
enemySpots.note: Campers sit in the spawn corners; the porch has good peeks and attracts thrown equipment.

maps.trap: Back rooms. It's one of the four choke points and it should be avoided — but it's also the quickest route to the porch, which is exactly why people keep taking it and keep dying in it. The porch itself then attracts thrown equipment, so the fast route punishes you twice.

loadout.weaponWhy: The control room is a bottom-and-top SMG fight with short peeks — 3-shot kill to 19.5m and a 0.2s aim-in suits it.
loadout.perkWhy: Half a dozen entrances to one room means people arrive from everywhere. Footsteps are the only warning you get.

deeper: A Motion Sensor in the right corner of the control room covers four popular choke spots at once — the highest-value piece of equipment on this map.
Toss a flash into middle hall; it very reliably catches people.
Breaking the glass in top control room changes the room — it becomes one of the biggest spaces on the map, with far more angles than people expect.
Double barrels gives a view of the Spetsnaz spawn buildings.
Constant pressure matters more here than on bigger maps: pushing the enemy back is what keeps your spawns favourable.
Lethal grenades and gas into the upper room of the compound shake people out of it.
verified: One of the smaller maps, with four major choke points, each involving the control room (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
On a map this size you must keep pushing the enemy to hold favourable spawns (ZigZack)
The control room is the centre: multiple levels, multiple windows, about half a dozen entrances (ZigZack)
A motion sensor in a corner of the control room covers four popular choke spots (ZigZack)
Back rooms is a choke to avoid, but the quickest route to the porch; the porch attracts thrown equipment (ZigZack)
Top control room is a hot spot and one of the bigger rooms once the glass is broken (ZigZack)
A flash into middle hall reliably catches players (ZigZack)
The back area is underused and watches nearby spawn points; the back stairs are underrated (ZigZack)
The Black Ops spawn balcony gives a clear view of major spawn points (ZigZack)
The rock area is the sniper route, with a long view down the west side; double barrels views the Spetsnaz spawn buildings (ZigZack)
A skinny bridge leads to the back of the Spetsnaz spawn; snipers shoot through the trees there (ZigZack)
Around or through the electrical room is a quick route to the porch, and a grenade magnet (ZigZack)
The centre compound is where most kills occur; grenades and gas into the upper room work (Dominate Black Ops)
Set in the Ural Mountains with severe drops on all sides (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Radiation
maps.identity: One of the fastest maps in the game. Most firefights happen outdoors, there are gates in the middle either team can open or close, and a basement tunnel underneath that can cut the map in half if you dare use it.

sides.name: Spetsnaz
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side, by the shipping room — a couple of camping spots and some spawn points, but not much action.
sides.opening: Use the red barrels at the start of the round; they set up multi-kills. A quick flash tells you if anyone is heading your way.
sides.flank: The tower walkways behind the shipping room, or the lookout for elevated shots down the centre.
sides.pinch: The tower walkways themselves — long and narrow, with nowhere to go if you meet someone.

sides.name: Black Ops
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side — fairly wide open, with lots of little nooks and crannies.
sides.opening: Climb the forklift. It gives a clear view of the centre of the map and of bottom reactor room, and it's one of the best-value spots here.
sides.flank: The second shipping room on this side leads down into the tunnel.
sides.pinch: The nooks and crannies themselves. They're fun and they'll quietly restrict you to one end of the map if you let them.

powerPositions.name: The upper control room
powerPositions.why: Sees the inside and the middle of the map clearly, and it holds the switch that opens the middle gates — so it's both a firing position and map control.

powerPositions.name: The forklift climb
powerPositions.why: A clear view of the centre and of bottom reactor room from one spot.

enemySpots.name: Centre reactor room
enemySpots.note: Explicitly a spawn haven — expect people to appear there, not just pass through.

enemySpots.name: The lookout and the fan area
enemySpots.note: Both elevated: the lookout covers the centre, the fan area covers players spawning Black Ops side.

enemySpots.name: The roof
enemySpots.note: Useful when pushing toward their spawn, but whoever is up there is out in the open.

maps.trap: The basement tunnel, if you treat it as a safe route. It has wide open spaces and five access points, and moving through it quickly genuinely cuts the map in half — but it is almost as unsafe as running through the centre. The other one is the back side of the reactor room, a major choke where you should expect grenades and flashes.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m with good handling — most fights here are outdoors at medium range.
loadout.perkWhy: On the fastest map in the game, the flank only works if it's not announced.

deeper: This is a pressure map: the team constantly pushing gives their opponents genuinely terrible spawns. Momentum matters more here than position.
The large gates in the middle can be controlled from either side of the map and can swing a game — the control room switch opens them.
The conveyor belt in the reactor room leads to a catwalk lining the back of the room.
From the gates you can peek across to the double windows.
Lower Spetsnaz spawn has a few camping spots but is otherwise fairly empty.
verified: One of the fastest maps: constant pressure gives opponents terrible spawns (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Most firefights are outdoors, but a basement tunnel can create game-changing momentum (ZigZack)
The Spetsnaz shipping room has camping spots and spawn locations but little action; tower walkways behind it are long and narrow (ZigZack)
Red barrels at the start of every round set up multi-kills; a quick flash reveals incoming players (ZigZack)
Large gates in the middle can be controlled from either side of the map (ZigZack)
You can peek across to the double windows (ZigZack)
The Black Ops spawn has a second shipping room leading to the tunnel, and is wide open with many nooks (ZigZack)
Climbing the forklift gives a clear view of the centre and bottom reactor room (ZigZack)
A conveyor belt leads to a catwalk lining the back of the reactor room; centre reactor room is a spawn haven (ZigZack)
The upper control room sees the inside and middle of the map, and holds the switch for the middle gates (ZigZack)
The fan area gives an elevated position on players spawning Black Ops side; the roof is useful but exposed (ZigZack)
The back side of the reactor room is a major choke point for grenades and flashes (ZigZack)
The Spetsnaz lookout gives elevated shots across and down the centre; lower Spetsnaz spawn is fairly empty (ZigZack)
The basement tunnel has wide open spaces and five access points, and is almost as unsafe as the centre (ZigZack)

maps.name: Jungle
maps.identity: A quick map with surprisingly long views, so almost any gun works. Two camps either side, two bridges between them, and a sniper perch that is one of the strongest scoping positions in the game.

sides.name: SOG
sides.spawn: The SOG side — and it gives the quickest access to the sniper perch.
sides.opening: Go straight to the sniper perch. It's a big enough area to move around in while scanning most of the map, so you can dodge tossed grenades rather than just eat them.
sides.flank: Out of SOG camp to the small bridge, one of the few crossings into NVA territory.
sides.pinch: The small bridge. It's one of the busiest spots on the map and it gets narrow.

sides.name: NVA
sides.spawn: The NVA side, around the camp and its blown-out buildings.
sides.opening: Use the elevated and long-shot positions in the heart of the spawn — there are a few that see deep across the map.
sides.flank: Through the rebel area, where most things are climbable.
sides.pinch: The choke just past the small bridge — enemies and teammates arrive from all sides, so pick a route and keep moving rather than trying to hold it.

powerPositions.name: The jungle sniper perch
powerPositions.why: Called one of the strongest spots to get scope shots off in the entire game. Big enough to outmanoeuvre grenades while scanning most of the map.

powerPositions.name: The back tree
powerPositions.why: A fun, underused spot with excellent camouflage and a view over most objectives.

enemySpots.name: The back areas of the NVA spawn
enemySpots.note: People camp them, and in most modes the objective sits around there.

enemySpots.name: Elevated positions over the middle route
enemySpots.note: The straight-through-the-middle route is shot down into from above.

enemySpots.name: The blown-out buildings in NVA camp
enemySpots.note: Enemies push through them constantly.

maps.trap: Getting pushed back into your spawn points. On a map this quick, if your team is under pressure you start spawning all over the place rather than moving through the map, and it's very hard to recover. The middle bridge is the other one — it cuts the map in half and it's the fastest route, but you cross it with almost no cover.

loadout.weaponWhy: The map offers long views down its length, so reach pays — 3-shot kill to 45.7m. Run a Grip.
loadout.perkWhy: The crossings are watched; taking one unannounced is the difference.

deeper: SOG camp is a very popular spawn area and it's easy for the enemy to pin you in it when your team is under pressure.
Both sides of the central route offer rocks and barrels to hide behind — the route is dangerous but it isn't coverless.
Most things in the rebel area are climbable, which opens angles people don't check.
Despite the foliage this map supports long-range weapons well, so don't automatically reach for an SMG.
verified: A very quick map; if your team is being pushed you spawn all over rather than moving through it (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Offers long views down the map, making just about any gun usable (ZigZack)
The SOG spawn gives the quickest access to the sniper perch (ZigZack)
The jungle sniper perch is one of the strongest scoping spots in the game, and big enough to outmanoeuvre thrown grenades (ZigZack)
SOG camp is a popular spawn area where teams under pressure get pinned (ZigZack)
The small bridge is one of the busiest spots and one of the few crossings into NVA territory; it narrows (ZigZack)
Past it is another popular choke where players arrive from all sides (ZigZack)
The middle bridge cuts the map in half and is fast but nearly coverless (ZigZack)
NVA camp has blown-out buildings enemies constantly push through; the NVA spawn's back areas are camped and hold most objectives (ZigZack)
The back tree gives amazing camouflage and a view over most objectives (ZigZack)
Most things in the rebel area are climbable (ZigZack)
The straight-through-the-middle route has rocks and barrels for cover but is shot into from elevated positions (ZigZack)
Classified as a large map by Treyarch; a ruined village and a military base split by a river (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Hanoi
maps.identity: A straightforward map with only two levels to it, which makes watching your back much easier than usual. Two central areas carry the fighting, and the second-level buildings looking down on them decide who moves freely.

sides.name: SOG
sides.spawn: The SOG side — quieter than the other end, because the back house shields most of the area.
sides.opening: Take a second-level building overlooking a central area. Controlling those is what unlocks the quicker routes across the map.
sides.flank: Down the far side toward the NVA spawn, using the trucks for cover and vision.
sides.pinch: The far side itself — it's home to many spawns and popular camping areas, so you rarely get down it uncontested.

sides.name: NVA
sides.spawn: The NVA side, a much busier spawn area than SOG's, around a long street-like open space.
sides.opening: Rush to the sides. The long street has very little cover in the middle, and a building plus a few elevated positions make this spawn hard to take over.
sides.flank: Round to the narrow side of the map, where passages and doorways make for close encounters.
sides.pinch: Those narrow passages. They're where the chokes really are — good if you're set, bad if you're moving.

powerPositions.name: The back balcony
powerPositions.why: A favourite spot, and there's a quirk: the railing is bugged and bullets don't penetrate it, so it gives cover it shouldn't.

powerPositions.name: Second-level buildings over the central areas
powerPositions.why: They look down on the ground where the fighting happens, and holding one is what gives your team the quicker routes.

enemySpots.name: The well area
enemySpots.note: Home to most objectives, and getting a shot off on anyone controlling it is difficult.

enemySpots.name: The far side of the map
enemySpots.note: Many spawns and popular camp areas along it.

enemySpots.name: The high building areas
enemySpots.note: They look down into the central areas, which have little cover.

maps.trap: The central areas. There isn't much cover in them and you're being looked down on from the high buildings, so cutting through the middle is the fast route from one end to the other and the unsafe one. On a map with only two levels, the danger is almost always from above rather than from a surprise angle.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 21m and a fast aim-in for the narrow passages and close encounters.
loadout.perkWhy: Close trades through doorways and thin walls, where reduced flinch decides who wins.

deeper: Only two levels to the whole map means fewer nooks for people to appear from — you can watch your six far more reliably here than on Summit or Villa.
The flower pot gives angles from a position enemies usually don't expect.
The back courtyard peeks onto people pushing out of the central areas.
The SOG back roof is a fun camping spot, but there isn't much action in that corner.
The night sky makes Spy Planes hard to spot and shoot down, so they last longer here.
verified: A straightforward map with only two levels, making it easier to watch your six while pushing (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Two central areas carry the fighting; controlling the second-level buildings above them gives quicker routes (ZigZack)
The SOG spawn has camp spots like the back roof but little action, because the back house protects the area (ZigZack)
The well area holds most objectives and is hard to shoot into (ZigZack)
The back balcony's railing is bugged — bullets do not penetrate it, giving free cover (ZigZack)
The back courtyard peeks at people pushing from the central areas (ZigZack)
The trucks on the far side give outstanding cover and vision; the far side has many spawns and camp areas (ZigZack)
The NVA spawn is busier than SOG's: a long, wide-open street with cover only at the sides, plus a building and elevated positions that make it hard to take (ZigZack)
The opposite side of the map is much narrower, with passages and doorways making close encounters (ZigZack)
The flower pot gives unexpected angles (ZigZack)
The central areas have little cover and are overlooked from the high buildings; most fighting is at ground level (ZigZack)
A North Vietnamese prison based on the Hanoi Hilton, set at night; the dark sky makes Spy Planes hard to spot (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Havana
maps.identity: A Cuban street with two near-identical buildings — the cigar shop and the hotel — facing each other across Main Street. Both have second levels that see most of the opposite side, and the street between them is the thing to avoid.

sides.name: Tropas
sides.spawn: Behind the bus, on the Tropas side.
sides.opening: Move around the map rather than through Main Street. The sniper house to the right of spawn looks straight down it — use that instead of walking it.
sides.flank: Into the cigar shop, which has many entrances, and up to the second level. From there you see the bus, the bar and the hotel.
sides.pinch: Crossing the street. If you have to do it, do it quickly — the sniper house and both second levels cover its length.

sides.name: OP 40
sides.spawn: The OP 40 end, reached through the shelter.
sides.opening: Take the hotel and get upstairs. It's laid out like the cigar shop and its second level sees the shelter, the fountain, the cafe and the cigar shop.
sides.flank: Stairs from the hotel into the back alley and round to the bar.
sides.pinch: The red rooms. They get congested with grenades and knifers — cross carefully.

powerPositions.name: Second level of the cigar shop
powerPositions.why: Eyes on the entire opposite side of the map — the bus, the bar and the hotel all at once. Many entrances below it, so it's reachable from several directions.

powerPositions.name: Second level of the hotel
powerPositions.why: The twin of the cigar shop, covering the majority of the other side: the shelter, the fountain and cafe, and the cigar shop itself.

enemySpots.name: The sniper house
enemySpots.note: Right of the Tropas spawn, looking down Main Street. The signature Havana angle.

enemySpots.name: The back rooms
enemySpots.note: Home to campers — but don't ignore them, they're worth clearing.

enemySpots.name: The fountain
enemySpots.note: Great cover, and it gets a lot of action. Expect company.

maps.trap: Main Street. The whole map is built so that both second levels and the sniper house look down it, which is why the advice is to move around the map rather than through the middle. If you must cross, cross fast and cross once.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot burst kill out to 58.4m — the reach that makes the second-level holds pay.
loadout.perkWhy: The route around the outside is the good one, and it only works if you're off their minimap.

deeper: A motion sensor in the trash bags tells you what's coming toward the fountain — a specifically recommended placement.
The dumpster is an underrated spot: it looks at the back of the fountain, the hotel, the sniper house and the shelter from one position.
The back cafe peeks over the fountain, so you can contest it without standing in it.
The shelter is the route to the OP 40 spawn — useful to know both for flanking and for understanding where they'll come from.
If you run a suppressor here the M16 drops from a 3-shot kill at 58.4m to 26.4m, which undoes the reason to hold a second level.
verified: It's important to move around the map rather than through Main Street (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Tropas spawn is behind the bus; a sniper house to the right of it looks down Main Street (ZigZack)
The bar sits on a corner and sees the first and second levels of the cigar shop (ZigZack)
The cigar shop has many entrances, one leading to the fountain; its second level sees the bus, bar and hotel (ZigZack)
The back cafe peeks over the fountain; the fountain gives great cover but attracts action (ZigZack)
A motion sensor in the trash bags warns what's coming (ZigZack)
A dumpster spot views the back of the fountain, the hotel, the sniper house and the shelter (ZigZack)
The shelter leads to the OP 40 spawn; the back rooms are home to campers (ZigZack)
The red rooms get congested with grenades and knifers (ZigZack)
The hotel has a similar layout to the cigar shop; its second level sees the shelter, fountain, cafe and cigar shop, with stairs to the back alley and the bar (ZigZack)
The map is the same shape as Crossfire from Call of Duty 4 (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Grid
maps.identity: A snowy outdoor map built around two major buildings — the control room and the facility — and the close-quarters fighting between them. Relatively large, but it feels much smaller because of how many chokes it has.

sides.name: Spetsnaz
sides.spawn: The back hangar, opening out into the parking lot.
sides.opening: Up the stairs into the mid control room. Jump onto the railing and you can peek down the long alley through the trees.
sides.flank: Down the alley into the facility, then up to its second floor for angles on several sides of the map and across to the control room.
sides.pinch: The facility doorways. A popular choke and a popular claymore spot — check before you walk through.

sides.name: Black Ops
sides.spawn: Behind the facility, in a big open area.
sides.opening: Be careful leaving it — the open ground here is a haven for snipers, and most of them blend into the bushes.
sides.flank: Mid statue, then climb the ledge for an easy way straight into the second level of the control room.
sides.pinch: The back alley off the facility corners — it leads to a lot of spawn points, which cuts both ways.

powerPositions.name: The second floor of the facility
powerPositions.why: Angles onto different sides of the map at once, including across to the control room.

powerPositions.name: Second level of the control room, via the mid statue ledge
powerPositions.why: A climb most players don't take, into an area with several hiding spots that surprise people coming the normal way.

enemySpots.name: In the bushes by the Black Ops open area
enemySpots.note: Snipers blend into them — this is the map's sniping ground.

enemySpots.name: The facility corners
enemySpots.note: A lot of players lurk there; peek them rather than walking past.

enemySpots.name: The mid control room and its railing
enemySpots.note: It peeks the long alley through the trees.

maps.trap: Treating it like a big map. Grid is relatively large but plays much smaller because of its many chokes — the doorways, the alley and the corners are where games are decided, not the open ground. Walking the open area outside the Black Ops spawn is the specific mistake, because it's sniper country.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m handles the outdoor sightlines while staying usable in the two buildings.
loadout.perkWhy: With snipers holding the open ground, staying off the minimap is what lets you rotate at all.

deeper: The propane tanks give good cover in the parking lot area, and there's a crack you can shoot through to catch enemies using the red barrel.
From the Spetsnaz spawn you can use the rooftop to patrol opposite sides of the map and watch for flankers.
The second level of the control room has quite a few hiding spots — good for a surprise, bad if you get comfortable.
In TDM this map is often quieter than in the objective modes, which makes stealth approaches unusually effective.
verified: An outdoor snow map revolving around two major buildings and the close encounters between them (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Relatively large but feels much smaller because of its many chokes (ZigZack)
Spetsnaz spawn in a back hangar opening onto a parking lot, with stairs up to the mid control room (ZigZack)
Jumping on the control room railing peeks down the long alley through the trees (ZigZack)
Propane tanks give cover; a crack lets you shoot enemies using the red barrel (ZigZack)
The facility doorways are a popular choke and a claymore spot; players lurk around its corners (ZigZack)
A back alley off those corners leads to a lot of spawn points (ZigZack)
The facility's second floor gives angles on different sides and across to the control room (ZigZack)
Behind the facility is the Black Ops spawn: a big open area that is a haven for snipers, who blend into the bushes (ZigZack)
Mid statue has a climbable ledge giving easy access to the second level of the control room, an area with several hiding spots (ZigZack)
A rooftop at the Spetsnaz spawn lets you patrol opposite sides and watch for flankers (ZigZack)
Often quiet in Team Deathmatch and open to stealth play (Dominate Black Ops)

maps.name: Array
maps.identity: One of the larger maps, and more varied than it looks — a handful of routes that mix long-range fragging with close gun battles around a big open centre. Just about any weapon is usable here.

sides.name: Black Ops spawn
sides.spawn: The Black Ops end, off a huge open area.
sides.opening: A quick grenade at the doorway by the truck at the start of the round can get multiple kills — it's a major choke and people funnel there.
sides.flank: Toward centre array via the pallet and forklift, then the guard house.
sides.pinch: The stairs above the guardhouse. They're narrow, so it's a kill or be killed — and watch for claymores on them.

sides.name: Opposite spawn
sides.spawn: The far end, toward the crane.
sides.opening: The large crane gives a couple of levels and huge peeks down the side of the map. Take a look, take a kill, then move — good players work you out quickly.
sides.flank: The back tunnel in bottom array. It's underused and it gets you behind their lines fast.
sides.pinch: The open ground below the electrical tower. It's wide open and gets picked on constantly from centre array.

powerPositions.name: The legs of the electrical tower
powerPositions.why: You can jump onto them for excellent cover while keeping good peeks on the open ground — one of the best-value spots on the map, and it fixes the problem that the area below the tower is otherwise a shooting gallery.

powerPositions.name: Centre array, reached by climbing the boxes
powerPositions.why: Climbing up to centre array lets you avoid all the popular routes and chokes where you're most likely to be killed. Best ground, safest arrival.

enemySpots.name: Array Tower
enemySpots.note: The map's landmark and where people camp. The bunkers and trucks in the open area are the cover you use to get angles on them.

enemySpots.name: Under the wedge, by the hill
enemySpots.note: A specific camping spot. If you're on the hill, move fast and keep your eyes on it.

enemySpots.name: The crane and the satellite dish
enemySpots.note: Both climbable, both give long peeks — the dish looks down the electrical tower.

maps.trap: The open ground below the electrical tower. It's wide, it's overlooked from centre array, and it gets picked on by a lot of people. The rock area is the other one — a strong choke that's surrounded by spawns, so you can win a fight there and immediately have company.

loadout.weaponWhy: 58.4m of 3-shot kill range for the long routes — though Array genuinely supports anything, so bring what you shoot well.
loadout.perkWhy: Rotations are long, and the back tunnel only works as a flank if you aren't on their minimap while you take it.

deeper: The truck at the doorway won't blow up, so the back of it is genuine cover. Once it has been destroyed, the wreck becomes an elevated position with angles into both spawns.
The unfinished building has thin walls that will get you killed, but it offers a useful peek if you're just passing through.
You can jump onto a ledge in the ice cannon and be out of range of most grenades and bullets while prone.
Jumping out of the window onto the railing gives a spot that peeks the propane tank and the main entrance of Array Tower.
Claymores are common on the guardhouse stairs and in the rooms — check before you move through.
The pallet and forklift lead to the guard house; both are critical choke points for traffic.
Don't run a suppressor here. Cutting your full-damage range on a map this open is self-sabotage.
verified: One of the larger maps, offering a handful of routes for both long-range and close combat; just about any weapon is usable (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
A large open area with bunkers and trucks providing cover for angles on players camping in Array Tower (ZigZack)
A major choke at the truck by the doorway; a grenade at the start of the round can multi-kill; the truck won't blow up so its back is cover (ZigZack)
Once destroyed, the truck becomes an elevated position with angles into both spawns (ZigZack)
Players camp under the wedge near the hill (ZigZack)
A large crane offers a couple of levels and long peeks down the side of the map (ZigZack)
The satellite dish is climbable and peeks down the electrical tower; the unfinished building has thin walls but a useful peek (ZigZack)
The rock area is a strong choke point surrounded by spawns (ZigZack)
The stairs above the guardhouse are narrow and claymored; the pallet, forklift and guard house are critical traffic chokes (ZigZack)
A ledge in the ice cannon puts you out of range of most grenades and bullets when prone (ZigZack)
The area below the electrical tower is wide open and gets shot from centre array; jumping onto the tower's legs gives cover with good peeks (ZigZack)
Climbing the boxes to centre array avoids the popular routes and chokes (ZigZack)
A window-to-railing spot peeks the propane tank and the main entrance of Array Tower (ZigZack)
A back tunnel in bottom array is underused and gets you behind enemy lines quickly (ZigZack)
Centred on a large relay dish with surrounding buildings; large open areas make sniping prevalent (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: WMD
maps.identity: A fairly large snowed-in facility with real verticality — silos, a factory, catwalks, rafters and a middle house you can see most of the map from. Height is the whole game here.

sides.name: Spetsnaz (silos)
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side, below the silos.
sides.opening: Climb the elevated positions below the silos and use the distance. The sniper perch by the AC unit gives good cover and watches the middle.
sides.flank: Into the factory, which has three major entrances — from there you either watch players crossing the middle or watch for flankers.
sides.pinch: Crossing the middle in view of the silos. The elevated positions on that side exist precisely to punish it.

sides.name: Black Ops
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side.
sides.opening: Climb the ladder to the rafters — the most elevated position on the map. You can cover teammates from there and alternate between firing spots to keep the enemy guessing.
sides.flank: Cut through cat house to middle house, either jumping across or climbing from the ground up.
sides.pinch: The catwalk peek. It gives a wide view into the Black Ops spawn, which means it also looks straight back at you.

powerPositions.name: The rafters, above the Black Ops spawn
powerPositions.why: The most elevated position on the map, with enough spots to alternate your fire from so nobody pins down where you are.

powerPositions.name: The second level of middle house
powerPositions.why: A 360-degree view of most of the map. The ground floor is a death trap with four entrances; the level above it is the reason to go there at all.

enemySpots.name: The warehouse overlooking the silos
enemySpots.note: Explicitly a camper's haven. From its top there's a clear view of the whole silo area.

enemySpots.name: The sniper perch by the AC unit
enemySpots.note: Good cover watching the middle. Assume it's occupied before you cross.

enemySpots.name: The factory's three entrances and the catwalk
enemySpots.note: Both watch the middle crossings and the flank routes.

maps.trap: Playing middle house on the ground floor. It has four main entrances, which makes it a very risky area — you cannot watch them all, and people arrive from every side. The second level is what you actually came for; the ground floor is where you die.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m with manageable recoil — the lanes are long enough to punish an SMG without demanding a full long-range build.
loadout.perkWhy: The flank routes through cat house and the factory only work if they can't see you take them.

deeper: The stairs give good cover against players rushing out of the Black Ops spawn, especially against the cat house windows.
Verticality is the point of this map: silos, sniper perch, factory, catwalk, rafters and middle house's upper level are all elevated. Before you cross anything, look up.
A freight train passes on the west-side railway at random times — noise cover that works both ways.
The catwalk is reached by ladder and sees a good portion of the map, but it is a known route rather than a hidden one.
verified: A fairly large map (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
Below the silos there are elevated positions to climb and use the distance from (ZigZack)
A sniper perch with an AC unit gives cover and watches the middle of the map (ZigZack)
The factory has three major entrances and watches both the middle crossings and flankers (ZigZack)
A ladder leads to the catwalk, which sees a good portion of the map and peeks into the Black Ops spawn (ZigZack)
A ladder in the Black Ops spawn leads to the rafters — the most elevated position on the map, with multiple firing spots (ZigZack)
Cat house connects to middle house; you can jump across or climb from the ground (ZigZack)

maps.name: Launch
maps.identity: Not actually a small map, though it plays like one because everybody forces the same few routes. The middle is split in two by railroad tracks and is deeply unstable — this is a team map, and solo heroics do not get through enemy lines.

sides.name: Spetsnaz
sides.spawn: The Spetsnaz side. The back area behind it is wide open with a handful of spawn points — which is exactly why air strikes land there.
sides.opening: Push up the left side toward the middle, but expect it: that's the most popular choke breaching this spawn, and it will be full of grenades and flashes.
sides.flank: Bottom rocket into the three-storey area, which takes you up to top rocket with one press of sprint.
sides.pinch: The left-side choke. If you get through the nades and flashes you reach the centre — plenty don't.

sides.name: Black Ops
sides.spawn: The Black Ops side. More confined, which funnels foot traffic into a single area.
sides.opening: Push out. Getting spawn trapped here is very hard to recover from, so the priority is not letting it start.
sides.flank: The mirrored bridge, or the identical three-storey route on this side of the rocket for long peeks on enemies spawning opposite.
sides.pinch: The back rooms of your own spawn — a popular spot for enemy equipment. Check for claymores and tactical insertions.

powerPositions.name: Top rocket, via the three-storey area
powerPositions.why: Both sides have an identical three-storey route from bottom rocket to top rocket that you clear with one press of sprint. The same jumps on the far side of the rocket give long-range peeks onto enemies spawning opposite.

powerPositions.name: The middle crossing that overlooks the centre
powerPositions.why: A major route into the Spetsnaz side, and it gets exceptional vision on anyone running straight through the middle.

enemySpots.name: Overlooking the middle
enemySpots.note: Most firefights start and end in the centre, and the routes across it are watched.

enemySpots.name: The back Black Ops spawn rooms
enemySpots.note: A popular area for equipment — claymores and tactical insertions rather than players.

enemySpots.name: The three-storey areas either side of the rocket
enemySpots.note: Both sides are identical, so whatever you're doing, they can do back.

maps.trap: The middle. It's split in two by the railroad tracks and it is almost impossible to watch every angle — most firefights and most deaths start and end there. Solo pushes through it are the specific thing this map punishes.

loadout.weaponWhy: 45.7m of 3-shot range handles the medium-long lanes without being useless inside the structures.
loadout.perkWhy: A lot of fights here are through structures and at ranges where flinch decides the trade.

deeper: The barriers in the middle are bulletproof — real cover, not decoration. Use them rather than sprinting between them.
Air strikes on the open back area of the Spetsnaz spawn are unusually effective because of the number of spawn points clustered there.
Getting spawn trapped in the Black Ops spawn is very difficult to recover from. If your team is being pinned, the answer is a coordinated push out, not individuals trying to break it.
The rocket launches around the halfway point and kills anyone beneath the engines — decide in advance where you'll be.
This map rewards playing with your team more than any other in the rotation.
verified: Not considered a small map, though most people feel like it is; plenty of routes exist but most players force the popular ones (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
A very unstable middle section makes it a team-oriented map where solo pushes fail (ZigZack)
The back area of the Spetsnaz spawn is wide open with a handful of spawn points — good for air strikes (ZigZack)
Pushing the left side reaches the most popular choke breaching the Spetsnaz spawn, defended with grenades and flashes (ZigZack)
The centre is split in two by railroad tracks, and the barriers there are bulletproof (ZigZack)
The Black Ops spawn is more confined with concentrated foot traffic; its back rooms are a popular equipment spot — check for claymores and tactical insertions (ZigZack)
Being spawn trapped in the Black Ops spawn is very hard to recover from (ZigZack)
Both sides have an identical three-storey area linking bottom rocket to top rocket, clearable with one sprint; the same route on the far side gives long peeks onto opposite spawns (ZigZack)

Most firefights and deaths start and end in the middle (ZigZack)

maps.name: Villa
maps.identity: A hillside estate with three elevated positions and a lot of connective ground between them. Tropas spawn mansion side at the pool, OP 40 opposite at the hill, and most of the game is about which house you own.

sides.name: Tropas (pool)
sides.spawn: Mansion side, at the pool.
sides.opening: You have immediate access to the middle and back roads and to the mansion. Take the mansion — it's home to many firefights and it's the best house on the map for a sniper or an assault rifle.
sides.flank: Middle towards the statue, which gives a great peek on the connector from a safe distance.
sides.pinch: The choke points past the fountain. Cutting the map from there is easy and quick, and it funnels you into a couple of tight spots.

sides.name: OP 40 (hill)
sides.spawn: The opposite side, at the hill.
sides.opening: Take the sniper house — one of the three elevated positions on the map, and valuable if you can shoot.
sides.flank: The back road, or through market via the stairs.
sides.pinch: The back exit toward your own spawn. Watch for flankers using the back road and campers sitting on the back hill.

powerPositions.name: The mansion
powerPositions.why: Home to many firefights and full of good spots. From it you get eyes right across the map to the sniper house and the lower connector — great cover with a lot of distance.

powerPositions.name: The sniper house
powerPositions.why: One of the three elevated positions on the map, and the natural counter-hold to the mansion.

enemySpots.name: The back hill
enemySpots.note: Campers sit on it, covering the approach to the OP 40 spawn.

enemySpots.name: The sniper house and the lower connector
enemySpots.note: The mansion looks at both, which means both look back.

enemySpots.name: The guard house, dirt road and fountain
enemySpots.note: Named hot spots where traffic concentrates.

maps.trap: The connector. The statue gives a great peek on it precisely because standing in it is bad — it's the ground the elevated positions are watching. The fountain route is the other one: it cuts the map quickly and runs you straight into a couple of chokes.

loadout.weaponWhy: 3-shot kill to 45.7m — the map rewards distance from the houses, and this covers it without dying indoors.
loadout.perkWhy: Back road flanks are a live threat in both directions; taking one unannounced is the difference.

deeper: The garage and the bar both lead back to the pool — useful for getting home, and for knowing how they'll come at you.
Double doors near the stairs lead through to the back road.
There are three elevated positions in total; the mansion and the sniper house are two of them, and holding one of those is most of the game.
Grenades roll downhill, which is in your favour from the mansion and against you from below.
verified: Tropas spawn mansion side at the pool; OP 40 spawn opposite at the hill (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
The Tropas spawn has immediate access to the middle and back roads and to the mansion (ZigZack)
The mansion is home to many firefights and suits snipers and assault rifles, with eyes across to the sniper house and the lower connector (ZigZack)
The guard house, dirt road and fountain are hot spots (ZigZack)
From the fountain you can cut the map easily but run into a couple of choke points (ZigZack)
One of those chokes leads to the sniper house, one of the three elevated positions on the map (ZigZack)
The back exit leads to the OP 40 spawn; watch for flankers on the back road and campers on the back hill (ZigZack)
Stairs give access to the back road and to market; double doors also lead to the back road (ZigZack)
The statue gives a great peek on the connector from a safe distance (ZigZack)
The garage and the bar both lead back to the pool (ZigZack)
A large house atop a cliff with a central courtyard of rock cover (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Crisis
maps.identity: One of the most versatile maps in the game — a close-quarters control room at one extreme and long-range beach fights at the other. Picking the right gun is genuinely tricky, because the terrain changes fast and the routes are quick.

sides.name: Tropas
sides.spawn: Plenty of cover here: a few buildings, jeeps, and the Rapunzel tower.
sides.opening: Wall jump to the upper level of Castro's house to skip the stairs, then overlook mid arches. From the side roof you watch the open area and the left flank.
sides.flank: Up the left flank through the shipping room, or through the jeeps using them as cover.
sides.pinch: The left flank itself — it's popular for spawn points, so you're likely to walk into people rather than past them.

sides.name: OP 40
sides.spawn: The OP 40 side, toward the beach, around the first rock perch.
sides.opening: Take the first rock perch. It oversees the open area ahead and puts eyes on the middle sandbags.
sides.flank: Across the beach to the second rock perch, which overlooks a side entrance to the control room.
sides.pinch: That side entrance area — it gets very congested, which is exactly why it produces multi-kills.

powerPositions.name: The middle sandbags, up the rock hill
powerPositions.why: Perfect for pushing back a team spawning beach side, and it oversees the entire section.

powerPositions.name: Upper Castro's house
powerPositions.why: Several entrances to the upper level, so you can arrive somewhere they aren't watching — and it overlooks mid arches.

enemySpots.name: The centre stairs of Castro's house
enemySpots.note: Most people still rush them despite the other entrances, making it a very popular choke.

enemySpots.name: The rock perches
enemySpots.note: Both overlook open ground — the first the open area and middle sandbags, the second a control room side entrance.

enemySpots.name: Bottom Castro
enemySpots.note: A very busy area with its own unique peeks.

maps.trap: The control room, if you take it for granted. It's filled with objectives in most modes and it cuts right through the map, making it the quickest route from the Tropas spawn to the OP 40 spawn — which is precisely why it's a hot spot and why everyone is already looking at it.

loadout.weaponWhy: 39.4m of 3-shot range with a 128ms kill — the compromise gun for a map that swings between the control room and the beach.
loadout.perkWhy: The left flank and the beach crossings are long enough that being on their minimap gets you killed before you arrive.

deeper: Just about any weapon is useful here — the real skill is playing to your gun's strengths rather than picking the 'best' one.
The back bridge leads into upper Castro, an alternative to the contested centre stairs.
Crossing to the Tropas spawn building gives access to the back control room.
The jeeps in the Tropas spawn are usable cover on the way up the left flank.

The first rock perch is an OP 40 spawn overseeing the open area with eyes on middle sandbags (ZigZack)

Up the rock hill are the middle sandbags — ideal for pushing back a team spawning beach side (ZigZack)
A back bridge leads into upper Castro; Castro's house has several upper entrances but most players rush the centre stairs, a very popular choke (ZigZack)
Bottom Castro is very busy with unique peeks; the Tropas spawn building gives access to the back control room (ZigZack)
The control room is a hot spot filled with objectives and cuts through the map, the quickest route between spawns (ZigZack)
A hidden missile facility in Cuba with indoor and outdoor battles and a beach (CoD Wiki)

maps.name: Cracked
maps.identity: Urban ruins where almost every area has multiple entrances, buildings run up to three storeys, and a lot of the good positions are reached by climbing. Nearly impossible to win unless your team keeps moving.

sides.name: NVA
sides.spawn: The NVA side — quite a few spawn points and a lot of camping areas.
sides.opening: Head to the second-storey house and jump out onto the awning for a view across whichever side you're pushing. Don't linger: there's very little cover up there.
sides.flank: Through the centre and climb into the nook, which gives a strong angle on enemies pushing.
sides.pinch: The main roads. Crossing on any of them is dangerous, especially once you're near their spawn buildings.

sides.name: SOG
sides.spawn: The SOG side, near the fruit market.
sides.opening: Get into the SOG lookout — either the normal way, or by jumping off the truck straight into the window.
sides.flank: The back area behind the fruit market, covering the middle and right sides.
sides.pinch: The climb into their spawn buildings — effective, but you're committed once you're up.

powerPositions.name: The blown-out building in the middle
powerPositions.why: It takes up the centre of the map, you can climb it to avoid the centre walkways, and controlling it gives you the upper hand. Watch for claymores on the second storey.

powerPositions.name: A third-storey peek
powerPositions.why: Climb to the third storey and there's a peek that produces long-range kills — unusual on a map people play at street level.

enemySpots.name: The NVA lookout
enemySpots.note: Usually has a sniper in it. Reachable by climbing the car or jumping across from the sandbags.

enemySpots.name: The second storey of the middle building
enemySpots.note: Commonly claymored rather than occupied.

enemySpots.name: Spawn-side camping areas
enemySpots.note: The NVA spawn in particular has many of them.

maps.trap: Standing still. Almost every area has multiple entrances, which makes holding anything nearly impossible — the map punishes teams that stop moving and rewards constant pressure. Crossing the main roads is the other reliable way to die, especially near their spawn buildings.

loadout.weaponWhy: Fast and accurate with 39.4m of 3-shot range — enough for the long peeks without losing the close fights.
loadout.perkWhy: Multi-storey buildings with multiple entrances mean people are constantly above, below and behind. Footsteps are the warning.

deeper: The rabbit hole is reached by climbing a crate — you can skip the double climb by sprint-crouching instead, which saves a couple of seconds.
The best way to push is to use the building openings and clear rooms as you move, rather than running the roads between them.
Climbing into an enemy spawn building lets you watch them advance up the map and shoot them in the back.
The map is the basis for the campaign mission The Defector and resembles Hue City.
verified: Most areas have multiple entrances, making it almost impossible to win unless your team is constantly moving (ZigZack, IGN map recon)
A variety of high angles, with buildings up to three storeys and many climbing spots (ZigZack)
The NVA spawn has many spawn points and camping areas (ZigZack)
From the second-storey house you can jump onto the awning for views across the map, but there is little cover there (ZigZack)
The middle is taken up by a blown-out building; climbing it avoids the centre walkways, its second storey is usually claymored, and controlling it gives the upper hand (ZigZack)
Crossing on the main roads is dangerous, especially near the opponent's spawn buildings (ZigZack)
You can climb into a spawn building and shoot enemies in the back as they advance (ZigZack)
A third-storey peek gives long-range kills (ZigZack)
The rabbit hole is accessed by climbing a crate; sprint-crouching avoids the double climb (ZigZack)
The SOG lookout leads to the fruit market on the SOG spawn side, with a back area covering the middle and right (ZigZack)
You can jump off the truck into the window as a quick route into the SOG lookout (ZigZack)

spawnSystem.how: The game puts you in the safest spot that isn't blocked by an enemy, and it re-reads where both teams are standing constantly. The practical version is the 70% rule: measure the distance from your spawn to theirs, and treat 70% of the way as the line you hold rather than cross.
spawnSystem.rule: Hold at 70% and the enemy is squeezed into the remaining 30% of the map, spawning in a small area you can watch. Cross it and you're deep in their half, you appear on the radar of everyone who has just spawned, and they will come looking for you.
triggers: Roughly three teammates pushing past the 70% line will flip the spawns
Even two of you at 80–90% is usually enough to trigger it
Wiping their whole side at once, leaving nowhere safe on their end
Standing on or near their spawn points
Leaning too heavily to one side — spawns can flip sideways, not just front to back
tells: A teammate dies and respawns right next to you while you're near the enemy spawn — the map has flipped, go back
Kills start arriving from a new direction
A part of the map that was busy goes quiet
spawnSystem.note: Spawn behaviour is more predictable on long, rectangular maps and less so on large, square ones. A Spy Plane makes it easy to see, but the skill is reading it without one.
spawnSystem.source: Pub-stomping fundamentals video covering Black Ops 1 and 2 (transcript supplied); corroborated for BO1 on Nuketown by a 2011 map guide describing enemies respawning behind your lines once your team pushes past the bus.
